summary: A reading of a 2023 lawsuit by former Twitter employees alleging that after buying the company in 2022, Elon Musk denied promised severance, staged pretextual firings, refused to pay rent and vendors, and ordered unsafe, code-violating work at its San Francisco headquarters.

evidence.note: Host introduces the complaint filed by former Twitter employees against Musk
Severance terms promised in the 2022 merger agreement
Mass layoff of November 2022 organised with Tesla and SpaceX engineers
Pretextual code reviews and performance plans used to fire staff for cause
Transition team says Twitter will not pay landlords or lease termination fees
Rent obligations questioned; janitorial staff left unpaid
December 2022 order that Twitter stop paying rent globally
Non-compliant locks and wiring in office sleep rooms endanger workers
California WARN Act and labor code claims tied to the San Francisco office
Complaint alleges layoffs targeted women, older and LGBT employees

notes: Format: the episode reads a legal complaint aloud, but media-reading is defined as a work made by a bastard; the plaintiffs are not, so current-affairs was chosen (lawsuit filed days before release, events of late 2022). Discrimination claims get only a short segment, so no bigotry theme. finance-crypto covers the lease and rent-default segment.
